question.problem:
$$
{f}_{Y|X}(y\,|\,-1)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{9}{4{y}^{13/4}}, & \,1\le y \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Let $X$ and $Y$ be continuous random variables. 
Find the conditional variance $\text{Var}[Y\,|\,X=-1]$ given that the conditional probability density function ${f}_{Y|X}(y\,|\,-1)$ is shown above and the corresponding expected value is ${\mu }_{Y|-1}=\frac{9}{5}.$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that the conditional variance of $Y$ given $X=x$ is defined by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[Y\,|\,X=x] & =\text{E}[(Y-{\mu }_{Y|x})^{2}\,|\,X=x] \\  & =\text{E}[{Y}^{2}\,|\,X=x]-{\mu }_{Y|x}^{2},\end{aligned}
$$

where 

$$
\text{E}[{Y}^{2}\,|\,X=x]={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }{y}^{2}\,{f}_{Y|X}(y\,|\,x)\,\text{d}y.
$$

Therefore, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{Y}^{2}\,|\,X=-1] & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }{y}^{2}\,{f}_{Y|X}(y\,|\,-1)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{\infty }{y}^{2}\cdot \frac{9}{4{y}^{13/4}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{\infty }\frac{9}{4{y}^{5/4}}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{\infty }\frac{9}{4}{y}^{-5/4}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={[\frac{9}{4}\cdot (-4)\cdot {y}^{-1/4}]}_{1}^{\infty } \\  & ={[-\frac{9}{\sqrt[4]{y}}]}_{1}^{\infty } \\  & =0-(-9) \\  & =9.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[Y\,|\,X=-2] & =\text{E}[{Y}^{2}\,|\,X=-2]-{\mu }_{Y|-2}^{2} \\  & =9-{(\frac{9}{5})}^{2} \\  & =9-\frac{81}{25} \\  & =\frac{144}{25}.\end{aligned}
$$
